briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 16, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Inequality
sections.content: Today, warnings about the direct impacts of climate change and deepening inequality continued across the globe. Domestically, a phenomenon where the wing color of blue butterflies fades due to climate change has been reported [2], and in Nepal, severe floods occurred, leading the Climate Change Action Research Institute to host a forum exploring climate disaster solidarity and responsibility [5, 9, 20], thus highlighting the issue of climate inequality once again. Internationally, California, USA, is experiencing a preview of the grim future of climate change due to the El Niño phenomenon [107, 128]; research suggests that climate change could lead to more toxic mine waste entering coastal waters [109]; an analysis indicates it fueled Hurricane Isaias [115]; and there's a point that the decisive role of climate change in modern wildfires should not be overlooked [113], among other factors identified as causes of various disasters. Notably, the UN has warned that millions of people in South Asia could be forcibly displaced due to climate change [120], and with an estimated economic loss of approximately 25 billion euros from Germany's 2026 heatwave [126], the economic and humanitarian costs of the climate crisis are escalating. Scientists warn that nearly half of coral reefs are at risk of extinction [131], and the puffin population in the UK is also threatened [127, 132], with pessimistic outlooks suggesting that the goal of limiting climate change to 1.5°C appears highly unrealistic [121].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality Policy Status
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts for climate change adaptation and achieving carbon neutrality are continuing, primarily led by local governments and institutions. Pukyong National University hosted a symposium to explore coastal ecosystem restoration and climate change response strategies [1, 3], and the National Climate Crisis Response Committee discussed policy directions through its 9th Climate Adaptation and Communication-Cooperation Subcommittee meeting [6]. Sangju City is developing customized climate change crisis response strategies [7]; the Rural Development Administration is preparing beekeeping farms for winter [8]; Pohang is developing customized rice varieties [16]; and Gimhae is providing blueberry farming education [17], among other agricultural adaptation efforts in response to climate change. Furthermore, Gyeonggi Provincial Library and Seongnam City are raising public awareness through climate crisis lectures and education [4, 22], and the Korea National Arboretum is actively engaged in educational and research efforts, including citizen science education through autumn leaves [10] and discussions on creating future value [13]. Nextmore Systems is promoting citizen safety by developing a climate safety service that helps locate shelters using heatwave map information [18].

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Controversies in Achieving Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Despite domestic and international efforts to achieve carbon neutrality, the process faces several challenges and controversies. At the Jeju Provincial Council, Seogwipo City's carbon neutrality projects were criticized for being 'forced' or for actually reducing emission reduction efforts [30, 35, 37, 38, 44]. Furthermore, despite the fuel tax cut policy continuing for five years, it was pointed out that carbon reduction has made no progress [43], and there was a suggestion that financial regulatory innovation is needed during the 'golden time for carbon neutrality' [36]. Despite the government's commitment to expanding renewable energy, criticism arose that, contrary to the 'triple expansion of renewable energy' announcement, grid connection remains uncertain for seven years [70], and a comparison was made that while renewable energy projects worth 1,000 trillion KRW are fast-tracked, new nuclear power plant construction undergoes a non-expert deliberation process [95]. In global supply chains, increasing demands for carbon neutrality are making rooftop solar panel installation mandatory for export companies [58, 100, 101], and this is even cited as a condition for the survival of small and medium-sized enterprises. These discussions demonstrate the importance of not just setting goals for the transition to carbon neutrality, but also ensuring practical implementation, transparent processes, and social consensus.

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy Expansion and Technological Innovation
sections.content: Efforts for technological development and infrastructure expansion for renewable energy transition are steadily progressing both domestically and internationally. Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) is collaborating with the Korea Meteorological Administration to advance renewable energy generation forecasting technology using meteorological data [80, 84, 92], and has also embarked on developing grid stabilization technology in preparation for the 100GW renewable energy era [72, 74]. Energy Storage Systems (ESS) are emerging as a core backbone of the power grid, overcoming the limitations of renewable energy [83]. Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) is contributing to Busan's carbon neutrality through the Dadaepo offshore wind power project [26] and is also initiating the development of next-generation BIPV (Building-Integrated Photovoltaics) technology [87]. Gyeongnam Provincial Office of Education is conducting training to strengthen new and renewable energy management capabilities for school administrative managers, raising awareness of energy transition among future generations [73, 77, 88, 89, 96], and Jeollabuk-do Province is promoting the expansion of household balcony solar power systems [99], striving to spread renewable energy in daily life. Furthermore, SK Oceanplant participated in a Taiwanese energy exhibition, showcasing its offshore wind power technology [90, 105], and international cooperation and technological exchange are active, with the groundbreaking of a wind farm also beginning in Munich, Germany [106]. The '2026 Asia-Pacific Renewable Energy Matching Forum' is scheduled to be held in Seoul, where discussions on RE100 and electricity market restructuring will take place [76, 85].

sections.title: 🌍 International Cooperation and AI Utilization for Climate Action
sections.content: International solidarity and the utilization of Artificial Intelligence (AI) are becoming increasingly important for responding to the climate crisis. KOICA is supporting developing countries in their climate crisis response by utilizing AI [11], and is hosting the 'Climate Action AI Forum' with UNFCCC to explore solutions through 'K-AI' [14]. As part of these efforts, a Tanzanian team achieved success by winning an international AI competition for climate crisis response [12]. At the upcoming COP31, AI is expected to be included in the agenda, deepening discussions on technology-driven climate action [129]. The European Union (EU) is achieving its nature and biodiversity targets set at COP17 [130], and following a UN request, approximately 58% of countries have submitted new pledges to address nature loss [136], demonstrating ongoing international efforts for nature conservation. This combination of international cooperation and advanced technology presents new possibilities for resolving the climate crisis.

briefing.closing: As we have observed in today's briefing, the severity of the climate crisis is increasing globally, but at the same time, innovative technological development, international cooperation, and practical efforts by local communities are being pursued in various ways to overcome it. We must confront and address the challenges for achieving carbon neutrality, and continue our steps towards a more sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
